Rank your house-hunting must-haves before you start viewing

Everyone's list of must-haves is longer than any house. Deciding which of two matters more (a shorter commute or a bigger garden?) tells you what to hold out for and what to give up when the right house is missing something.

Start ranking this list →

Opens the free ranker with the list below already filled in. Change it there with "Start over", or paste your own list.

The starter list

Question: "Which matters more in our next home?"

  1. Short commute
  2. Good schools nearby
  3. A garden or yard
  4. Off-street parking
  5. An extra bedroom
  6. A home office
  7. Walkable shops and cafes
  8. Quiet street
  9. Move-in ready, no renovation
  10. Lower price
  11. Natural light
  12. Close to family

Why picking pairs works here

  • Edit the list first: add the features you are actually weighing and remove the ones you don't care about.
  • If you are buying with someone, each answers alone and you combine codes; the table shows the features you split on.
  • The rank range says which places your answers settle and which are close calls, so you know where you are flexible.

What it doesn't do: It is a way to sort out preferences, not financial or property advice. Price, survey results and what you can borrow come first.

Compared with what you'd use today

Checklists from property sites and house-hunting worksheets. A checklist treats every item as yes or no; ranking pairs tells you which yes to trade away.

Under the hood: a Bradley-Terry model refit after every answer, an adaptive question picker, and a stop rule checked against simulated respondents, including ones whose picks are close calls. The method and its measurements.
